title: Time-Series Momentum 12-month, 19 futures, monthly rebalance
hypothesis: time-series momentum: long a market when its trailing return is positive, short when negative. Lookback 12 months skipping the most recent month, risk-scaled to equal volatility, rebalanced monthly. Classic, widely published rule; low turnover means the 1 bp + $4.50 cost model should matter far less than it does for the intraday gap rules.

rules.signal: score = sum of daily log returns over the lookback of 12 months excluding the last 21 trading days
rules.sizing: weight per market = sign(score) (tsmom) or +1/-1 by within-class rank (xsmom), times 10% target vol / 60-day realized vol, leverage capped at 3 per market, divided by number of active markets
rules.rebalance: last trading day of each month; weights decided at the close earn returns from the NEXT day

author: claude-proposer
disclosure: Menu candidate from the fixed canonical list; not selected on any result. Daily data starts 2010-06-08, so the first signal appears mid-2011 for a 12-month lookback. Roll-day returns are set to 0 (small understatement, see futures_daily.py).

pass_criteria.conditions: net Sharpe >= 0.3 in discovery AND net Sharpe >= 0.3 in validation AND validation cumulative net return > 0
pass_criteria.supported: conditions met AND validation Deflated Sharpe Ratio >= 0.95
pass_criteria.inconclusive: conditions met but the Deflated Sharpe Ratio is below 0.95
